args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service reports healthy on v2.3.0 in all three regions with a 0.2% error rate. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging before it went to production. Follow-up: find the root cause in v2.3.1 and work out why it was promoted despite failing in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's passing health checks again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **Problem:** The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was live in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks everywhere, with 18% of requests returning errors.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to that. All three regions are now on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and the on-call engineer has been paged. It describes the failure and the rollback, and lists follow-ups: finding the root cause in v2.3.1 and working out how it reached production.

v2.3.1's test build (v2.3.1-rc) was already marked unhealthy in staging before it went to production. That's worth looking into during the incident review.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
